key_insight: A nested homogenization strategy turns pore-scale xylem membrane geometry into an effective interface law, then into a conduit-scale closure for network-level flow exchange.
engineering_relevance: This provides a tractable multiscale model for predicting pressure drop and flow redistribution in porous fluidic networks without resolving every pore or prescribing ad hoc resistances.
method: Homogenize the rigid porous membrane to an effective stress-jump interface law at the pore scale.
Embed that interface in a second characteristic problem to derive conduit-scale pit-mediated exchange coefficients.
Propagate microgeometry to network-scale response through effective tensors in a xylem-inspired network model.
evidence_signal: The reduced model is validated against fully resolved simulations in simplified vessel connections and then tested in a network with randomly disabled conduits, matching pressure drop and flow redistribution trends.
watch_item: The framework is developed for rigid, single-phase membranes, so deformability, multiphase effects, and complex real-world tissue variability may require further extension.
paper_title: Nested homogenization of xylem-inspired porous fluidic networks
